protocol.description:
This protocol lets a client ask the compositor to apply an effect to whatever is behind a surface, most commonly a blur, so that a translucent surface reads as frosted glass rather than as a plain alpha blend.
Version 1 of this protocol is the upstream staging protocol unchanged: a client marks a region and the compositor decides everything else.
Version 2 is a local extension. Version 1 deliberately leaves the blur algorithm entirely to compositor policy, which is the right default but gives a client no way to distinguish a lightly frosted panel from a heavily obscured modal backdrop, and no way to have the blurred backdrop follow the rounded corners the surface is drawn with. Version 2 adds that control as hints the compositor is still free to clamp or ignore, and adds a way to say "the whole surface" without the client having to resend a region on every resize.
WARNING: version 2 is not part of the upstream protocol. A client must check the version of the bound global before using any version 2 request, and must be prepared for a compositor to only implement version 1.

interface.name: ext_background_effect_manager_v1
interface.description: This object is a factory for background effect objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Informs the server that the client will no longer be using this protocol object. Existing objects created by this object are not affected.

entry.name: background_effect_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a background effect object

entry.name: blur
entry.summary: the compositor supports blurring the background

event.name: capabilities
event.description: This event advertises the effects the compositor supports. It is sent once when the global is bound, before any other event.

request.name: get_background_effect
request.description:
Instantiate an interface extension for the given wl_surface to add background effects to it.
If the given wl_surface already has a background effect object associated, the background_effect_exists protocol error is raised.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: the surface to add effects to

interface.name: ext_background_effect_surface_v1
interface.description:
This interface allows a client to apply effects to the background of a surface.
All state set through this interface is double-buffered and applies on the next wl_surface.commit, so a client can change the blurred area, its strength and its corner rounding together with the frame that needs them and never show a mismatched intermediate state.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Informs the server that the client will no longer be using this protocol object. The effect is removed from the surface.

entry.name: surface_destroyed
entry.summary: the associated surface has been destroyed

request.name: set_blur_region
request.description:
This request sets the region of the surface that will have its background blurred.
The blur region is specified in the surface-local coordinates, and clipped by the compositor to the surface size.
The initial value for the blur region is empty. Setting the pending blur region has copy semantics, and the wl_region object can be destroyed immediately. A NULL wl_region removes the effect.
This supersedes any area previously set with blur_whole_surface.
The blur region is double-buffered state, and will be applied on the next wl_surface.commit.
The blur algorithm is subject to compositor policies.
If the associated surface has been destroyed, the surface_destroyed error will be raised.

request.name: blur_whole_surface
request.description:
Blur the background of the whole surface, whatever size it currently is.
This is equivalent to setting a blur region covering the surface, except that the compositor keeps it matched to the surface as the surface resizes. A client that wants its whole background blurred would otherwise have to compute and resend a region on every resize, and would show an unblurred or clipped frame whenever it got the ordering wrong.
This supersedes any region previously set with set_blur_region. Call set_blur_region with a NULL region to remove the effect again.
This state is double-buffered and applies on the next wl_surface.commit.
If the associated surface has been destroyed, the surface_destroyed error will be raised.

request.name: set_blur_radius
request.description:
Set how strongly the background should be blurred, as a radius in surface-local coordinates.
This is a hint. The compositor is free to clamp it to a range it can render efficiently, to quantise it, or to ignore it entirely; a client must not assume the result matches the value it asked for, and must not use this to convey anything but a visual preference.
A radius of 0 means the compositor should apply its own default strength, which is also the initial value. It does not mean "no blur" -- use set_blur_region with a NULL region for that.
This state is double-buffered and applies on the next wl_surface.commit.
If the associated surface has been destroyed, the surface_destroyed error will be raised.

arg.name: radius
arg.summary: blur radius in surface-local coordinates, 0 for the compositor default

request.name: set_region_radii

description.summary: round the corners of the blurred area

request.description:
Round the corners of the blurred area, so the backdrop follows the shape the surface actually draws.
Without this, a client drawing a rounded card over a rectangular blurred area shows blurred pixels poking out past its own corners. The client cannot fix that itself, because the blur is composited underneath it.
The array holds four unsigned 32-bit values per rectangle, in native byte order, giving the radii clockwise from top-left. The entries are index-matched to the rectangles of the region set by set_blur_region: a shorter array leaves the remaining rectangles square, and a single entry rounds every rectangle the same way, which is what a client blurring the whole surface means.
The radii are in surface-local coordinates. A compositor should clamp each radius so that adjacent corners cannot overlap.
All corners are initially square.
This state is double-buffered and applies on the next wl_surface.commit.
If the associated surface has been destroyed, the surface_destroyed error will be raised.

arg.name: radii
arg.summary: four uint radii per rectangle, clockwise from top-left
